title: Five upcoming meteor showers to grace night skies
excerpt: Here are a few meteor showers to put on your calendar, according to the American Meteor Society.
content:
If you missed the Perseids meteor shower in August, don’t despair. Here are a few more meteor showers to put on your calendar, according to the American Meteor Society:

  1. The Orionids:

This meteor shower stretches from Oct. 2 to Nov. 7, peaking on the night of Oct. 21-22. While this shower can produce about 50 to 75 meteors per hour during peak years, recent displays have been more humble. It’s also worth noting that the moon will be 80 percent full during the peak night, so the few hours between moonset and dawn will provide a more limited viewing opportunity.

  1. The Southern Taurids:

Set to take place between Sept. 20 and Nov. 20, this meteor shower actually includes two components – one that will peak on the night of Oct. 13-14 and a second that will peak on Nov. 4-5. While the second component is known for its fireballs during ‘swarm years,’ the American Meteor Society indicates that 2026 isn’t a ‘swarm year,’ thus the mid-October peak may actually bring the best chance to view this one. During the first peak night, the moon should be about 10 percent full, with the moon about 18 percent full during the second peak. Both the Southern and Northern Taurids (more on that below) tend to have less activity – about five to 10 meteors per hour.

  1. The Northern Taurids:

Coinciding with the Southern Taurids, the Northern Taurids meteor shower stretches from Oct. 20 through Dec. 10, peaking on the night of Nov. 11-12. On that night, the moon will be about seven percent full. The best viewing time will be after midnight, but again, expect five to 10 meteors per hour opposed to dozens.

  1. The Leonids:

Another meteor shower that will likely bring lower member numbers this year – around 10 to 15 an hour – the American Meteor Society reports this meteor shower will run from Nov 6-30. During the peak night – Nov. 16-17 – the moon will be about 45 percent full, though the American Meteor Society indicates this shouldn’t spoil the show for the best viewing time, which tends to be early morning hours.

  1. The Geminids:

This is probably the best upcoming chance to see meteor activity similar to that of the Perseids, with the Geminids producing up to 150 meteors per hour during its peak. According to the American Meteor Society, it will stretch from Dec. 4-17, peaking on the night of Dec. 13-14 when the moon is 21 percent full. Worth noting, however, is that the moon should be set by the time the Geminids are best viewed.

BONUS: The Perseids 2029:

While the Perseids meteor shower of 2027 and 2028 will be relatively obstructed by the glow of the moon, the Perseids meteor shower that’s set to peak around August 11 to 12, 2029 will occur when the moon is about five percent full. It’s not a new moon, but it’ll be about as close as it gets.
